extensions.tokenSyntax: Frontmatter values are normative QML expressions evaluated in Panel.qml context. Noor is default; System is optional.

display.purpose: Centered remaining time; horizontal fit minimum Style.space(34).

prayer-name.purpose: Arabic Kufi heading or English Noto Sans next-prayer name.

motion.name: settings-opacity
motion.purpose: Opacity only; visibility and height change immediately.

native.previewPolicy: Native QML references replace HTML/CSS approximations.
native.breakpoints: No web breakpoints; fitted content dimensions and vertical overflow.
native.campaignIntent: Architectural mihrab cut by sunlight with oversized title on ivory; separate from product UI.

components.name: Prayer window
components.description: Hairline, next prayer and exact start above centered light countdown and explanatory caption.

components.name: Prayer row
components.description: Compact native timetable row with aligned name, status and numeric time.

components.name: Next prayer row
components.description: Taller accent-washed row with bold name/time; fill intensifies when imminent.

components.name: Worldwide setup
components.description: Country and offline localized city selectors, regional method suggestion, manual override and search feedback.

components.name: Native settings
components.description: Appearance, contextual Habous, Hijri, coordinates, calculation and reminder controls.

components.name: Bar widget
components.description: Native active imminent state, language-aware font and three mouse actions.

narrative.overview:
Noor expresses the prayer window through generous numerals, intentional Arabic typography and a clear timetable. Deep emerald grounds warm ivory text; brass gold identifies the next prayer and its start. The centered light countdown is the primary answer, with a short caption explaining its meaning.

The implementation is native Qt Quick / Quickshell on Omarchy. Noor is the persisted default appearance; System colors are an explicit alternative. Campaign direction uses a sculptural mihrab and sunlight, separate from the working interface. The user rejected the former ring and generic screenshot-on-mosque cover.
keyCharacteristics: Typographic hierarchy with distinct Arabic heading and body families
Emerald, ivory and gold by default; optional live System colors
Clear aligned timetable with a taller next-prayer row
Flat native surfaces and restrained motion

rules.name: The Appearance Rule
rules.body: Preserve the Noor/System conditional bindings. Noor is an authored palette; System mode evaluates the current Omarchy colors instead of a screenshot palette.

rules.name: The Numeric Rule
rules.body: Keep schedule numerals right-aligned and unmirrored; apply reading alignment to language-bearing labels. Do not substitute a decorative clock face for the countdown.

dos: Do preserve Noor as default and System colors as an explicit alternative.
Do use the implemented Arabic heading/body families and Noto Sans numerals.
Do keep country selection and offline city setup visible before contextual Morocco controls.
Do keep native Qt Quick controls and Omarchy scale bindings.
donts: Don’t restore the rejected ring or a decorative clock face.
Don’t put screenshot-on-mosque artwork inside the working interface.
Don’t describe this native Linux panel as a web or mobile application.
Don’t add glow or a reveal that delays prayer information.
